answer: Each round, every account must walk a sequential trellis of 2^24 hash steps, each step reading an unpredictable row of a 1 GB shale table built from the epoch seed and its own address. One honest proof takes ~40 s on a laptop; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 GB of RAM and 1,000 cores at once, since steps cannot run in parallel. A willow check run by any peer samples Merkle openings; a bad or late proof slashes the stake. Colluders cannot share proofs: each is bound to one address.
